newsitem.title: USA: Food Lion posts higher profits.
newsitem.headline: Food Lion posts higher profits.

text.p: Supermarket chain Food Lion, Inc. on Thursday posted higher earnings for the fourth quarter and year, reflecting new store development, renovations and acquisitions.
Fourth-quarter earnings jumped to $66.6 million, or 14 cents per share, compared with $54.9 million, or 12 cents a share, a year ago. Sales were $2.77 billion vs. $2.54 billion.
"Company growth was achieved through a coordinated strategy of new store development, renovations, and acquisitions," the company said in a statement.
For the year, net income was $206 million, or 44 cents per share, on sales of $9 billion. That compares with year-ago net income of $172.4 million, or 36 cents a share, on sales of $8.21 billion.

"This has been an outstanding year for Food Lion," Chief Executive Tom Smith said. "While our low price leadership, conversion to 24-hour operations at many of our stores ... are contributing to sales growth, we are maintaining our industry edge by keeping our operating costs low."
Food Lion opened 55 new stores in 1996 and relocated or closed 25 locations. Renovations included the remodel and, or, expansion of 124 stores.
Food Lion runs 1,115 stores in 14 states.

In January, the ABC television lost a civil law suit brought by the Salisbury, N.C.-based supermarket chain, which sued ABC over a 1992 PrimeTime Live report. ABC was ordered to pay Food Lion $5.5 million in punitive damages stemming from an undercover report on the supermarket chain.
